decisive_items: The patient was initially acyanotic from 2010 to 2016, but gradually became cyanotic after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis
Revealed a patent foramen ovale measuring 7.34 mm in width with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt on colour flow mapping
Pulmonary artery pressure was 60/39 mmHg, lower than aortic pressure
response.rationale: Eisenmenger syndrome uniquely integrates chronic pulmonary hypertension, late cyanosis, and a right-to-left shunt through a congenital PFO; the other findings are secondary or incomplete.

rejected.why: PFO is the anatomical shunt but does not explain the pulmonary hypertension and cyanosis as a standalone diagnosis.
PAH is present but fails to account for the right-to-left shunt and cyanosis.
Contradicted by pulmonary angiography showing no pulmonary embolism or arteriovenous fistulae.
Tricuspid regurgitation is a secondary consequence of right heart remodeling, not the primary diagnosis.
